item.title: No guarantees: What do Kurds think of the Damascus-SDF agreement?
item.description: Kurds in northeastern Syria are cautiously waiting to see what comes next as Damascus and the SDF take their first steps towards a fraught integration.

item.title: Hasakah at a crossroads: Real integration, or recreating ‘security squares’?
item.description: As Damascus and the SDF inch towards integration, is northeastern Syria heading for unified state institutions, “complementary integration,” or a revival of divided influence?

item.title: Shutdown of Deir e-Zor's informal refineries upends a hazardous local economy
item.description: As the Syrian government shuts down Deir e-Zor's informal oil refineries, a local industry faces collapse even as nearby communities are likely to reap health and environmental benefits.

item.title: How olive oil exports exacerbate Syria’s water crisis
item.description: Even as Syria suffers an acute water crisis, thousands of cubic meters of groundwater are flowing into the global market in the form of olive oil, an export that represents both national pride and a silent depletion of resources.

item.title: ‘We lost everything’: How Israeli herbicides destroyed Quneitra crops and pastures
item.description: Israeli aircraft sprayed large areas of Syria’s southern Quneitra province with herbicides at least three times in late January, killing crops, devastating farmers and damaging trees.

item.title: Unspoken exclusion: Inaccessible public transport isolates disabled Syrians
item.description: An inaccessible public transportation system and degraded infrastructure pose daily challenges to disabled Syrians, isolating them and preventing their freedom of movement in an “unspoken form of social exclusion.”

item.title: One year after Syria’s coastal massacres, justice remains elusive
item.description: As Alawites mark one year since the massacres in Syria’s coastal regions, residents of Baniyas say fear persists, wounds remain unhealed and political demands unmet.

item.title: With rare movement in Suwayda-Damascus deadlock, can a solution emerge?
item.description: After months of deadlock, a prisoner swap between Damascus and Suwayda opened a “new” negotiating channel, but is there a way forward amid internal divisions and struggles over representation?

item.title: ‘A long way to go’: As Syrians commemorate the revolution, has it achieved its goals?
item.description: On the second anniversary of the revolution since the fall of the Assad regime, have its earliest aims—freedom, justice, dignity and the rule of law—been achieved, or is the journey far from over?

item.title: In southern Syria, echoes of the US-Israeli war with Iran hit close to home
item.description: While not a direct target of the escalating conflict between Israel, the US, Iran and Hezbollah, southern Syria is feeling its fallout—from drone debris to increased patrols by occupying forces.
